cb.setup: Four players. Three cards sealed in the envelope; you and Anna hold 5 cards, Ben and Cara hold 4. You go first.
cb.conservation: Every row sums to 1 — the card is somewhere. Every column has a fixed total: Anna 5, Ben 4, Cara 4, and the envelope holds exactly one per category. The Σ row is the expected number of cards of this category in each hand; the envelope column should read ≈1.00, sampling noise aside.
cb.showPrompt: {$name} suggested {$cards}. Show one card — which one leaks least?
cb.showTip: Tip: repeat a card you have shown them before — zero new bits.
cb.log.otherShows: {$shower} showed {$viewer} a card. You only learn the disjunction.
cb.log.nobodyYou: Nobody can disprove you. Anything you do not hold yourself is very likely in the envelope.
cb.log.nobodyBot: No one can disprove {$name}. Strong signal those cards sit in the envelope — or in their own hand.
cb.log.youHoldSeveral: You hold {$count} of those cards. Choose one to show {$name}.
cb.log.wrong: {$name} accuses {$cards} — WRONG. {$name} is out, but still must show cards.
cb.log.allOut: Everyone struck out. The envelope held: {$cards}.
cb.footnote: H is the Shannon entropy of the envelope distribution: it starts at log₂324 ≈ 8.3 bits, and you accuse near 0. Expected bits is H minus the probability-weighted entropy over every possible outcome of the suggestion. The model assumes a responder shows a card the suggester already knows about whenever they can — matching what the players actually do — so asking about a card you have located scores ~0 bits, and solved categories are probed with your own card or the deduced envelope card, which nobody can block.
